film.caption: Carrying, 2:04. The Arsenale and Castello, 22 October 2026
film.note: Sound on; captions in the player menu
p1: On the afternoon of 22 October one red unit left Tesa 41 on somebody’s back. It was strapped to a hiking frame with black webbing, and Aram Zadikian carried it out of the studio, along the quay, through the gate of the Arsenale and into the streets of Castello, with Zadik Zadikian walking beside him.
p2: It was a test, and a simple one: can a work from the pavilion be carried through Venice the way everything else in Venice is carried? It turned out to be the beginning of something larger.
fig.tesa-41-fitted: Aram Zadikian in Tesa 41 with the unit on his back, before setting out
p3: The unit is one of the studio’s plain forms: a tall red block, stepped at the shoulders, with a band of green at its foot. It is light enough for one person and big enough that the person all but disappears behind it. The afternoon began on the studio floor, tightening straps, kneeling to take the weight, standing up, walking a lap of the hall and adjusting again. The frame had had its first try in the hall eleven days before.
fig.first-fitting: 11 October: a first try of the back frame
fig.strapping: Zadik Zadikian checks the frame by the door of Tesa 41
p4: Then the door, and the quay, and the water.
fig.arsenale-quay: On the quay in front of the old boat sheds of the Arsenale
h2-by-hand: Everything by hand, or by boat
p5: The studio has spent the year learning what this city does to logistics; we wrote about it in Carried by Hand. Carrying a work through it on purpose turned that problem into the subject. As Aram puts it in the film:
quote-car: You don’t realise it until you can’t throw something in the back of your car or a truck and haul it to your destination. So everything has to be carried by hand, by boat.
p6: Zadik has always made work that goes out into the world: site-specific pieces, work set down outdoors, work taken out of the studio. This was the same impulse, with something new in it: the act of carrying weight. And the weight is not only the unit’s. Representing a country at the Biennale has a weight of its own; that day Aram called it “this cross you’re kind of bearing”.
p7: What surprised us was the street. A block of colour on someone’s back is about as basic a thing as you could carry, and yet nobody walks through Venice with anything like it. People stopped, turned, asked. “You don’t see something like this, of this scale, being carried around town,” Aram says. “How do you cut through with such a basic thing? Form, colour, that’s it.”
p8: Zadik saw it from the other side:
quote-tradition: It’s coming from a certain tradition, carrying. And yet in Venice it makes total sense, because there is no other way.
fig.portrait: Aram Zadikian in a campo in Castello, the unit on his back
p9: There was the wind, too. On the open quay a tall flat form becomes a sail, and the carrier learns quickly not to stand square to it. Somebody has to walk close by as a stabiliser. The film keeps that moment.
fig.setting-down: Setting the unit down on the quay, Zadik Zadikian watching
p10: One unit, one back, one afternoon. But the conversation on the way was already about more. “We want to do at least six,” Aram told someone who asked. “I have three more coming like this. It would be great if we had twenty.” Zadik agreed: six at least. Come out with six, he said, and there is no doubt what you are looking at.
p11: The studio had been building a flag in the hall, green, white and red, from the same kind of units, standing on its own feet. Units that can be carried one at a time can also be carried together. A flag could walk.
fig.back-in-tesa-41: Back in Tesa 41: Zadik and Aram Zadikian after the walk
p12: Zadik, at the end of the day, on a year of learning a new city: “Now maybe we learn some things. Let it go, have fun. Then it becomes very beautiful.”
p13: Two weeks later, three units went out together. That walk is The Weight of the Flag.
